note: Independent re-judge after 4ceb0f7416. Section 4.2.2 read in rfc/full/rfc6793.txt: "When communicating with an OLD BGP speaker, a NEW BGP speaker MUST send the AS path information in the AS_PATH attribute encoded with two-octet AS numbers." and "non-mappable four-octet AS numbers are represented by the well-known two-octet AS number, AS_TRANS." New positive TestRFC6996OldSpeakerReceivesStrippedASPathAndAS4Path asserts the exact AS_PATH octets 0204 fde8 fbf0 5ba0 fbf1 toward a two-octet EBGP peer on the real forward path: two-octet widths (a four-octet encoding changes every byte) and AS_TRANS 23456 for 65536. Break attribute/aspath.go:184 writeSegmentWithSplit as16=23456 -> uint16(asns[i]) (65536 truncates to 0) is the producing statement and was observed red. Claim states only what the bytes show. Existing units unchanged: TestRFC6793EncodeTwoOctetToOldSpeaker asserts a 2-octet AS_PATH with AS_TRANS toward a non-ASN4 context; the negative TestRFC6793TwoOctetASPathKeepsMappableASNs keeps mappable ASNs unsubstituted, so over-substitution is caught.
